articles.title: Katie Boulter crashes out of US Open after Karolina Muchova nightmare
articles.summary: British No 1 outclassed 6-1, 6-0 in second round. Boulter’s recent poor form continues in New York. With the grounds of the Billie Jean King National Tennis Centre at a standstill in the middle of a furious downpour and all eyes on the two stadium courts played under retractable roofs, there was…
body: This has been a life changing summer for Boulter, who married her fellow player Alex de Minaur in July. However, after a promising start to the season that saw her win her fourth WTA title in Ostrava and return to the top 60 after her brilliant win over the world No 2 Elena Rybakina at Queen’s, things have stalled.
Until her first round win in Cincinnati last month, she had lost five consecutive matches, including a painful straight-sets loss in the first round of Wimbledon. Confidence has been hard to come by.

Boulter and Muchova had initially been scheduled to compete on Court 17 after the men’s first round match between the rising star Rafael Jodar and Yunchaokete Bu, but as heavy rain suspended play with Jodar, the 12th seed, shockingly trailing the ­Chinese lucky loser 2-6, 1-6, 1-4, Boulter and Muchova were quickly moved to Louis Armstrong Stadium. She was completely outclassed by a sublime Muchova, who employed her usual brand of silky, all-court shotmaking, lasering forehand winners past the British No 1 and sweeping forward to the net.

articles.title: Clippers docked five first-round draft picks and fined $30m over Kawhi Leonard scandal
articles.summary: Team circumvented salary cap rules to sign star. Owner Steve Ballmer lands one-year ban. The NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Los Angeles Clippers after finding that the franchise circumvented salary cap rules when it courted Kawhi Leonard as a…
body: The league has stripped the team of five first-round draft picks, giving the team no natural pick in the draft from 2029 through 2033.

The NBA also fined the Clippers $30m, and suspended owner Steve Ballmer from all league and team activities for a year. In addition, it issued suspensions without pay to president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank (six months) and president of business operations Gillian Zucker (one year) for their involvement in the scheme.

Leonard was also fined $700,000. The Clippers agreed to trade the seven-time All-Star to the Toronto Raptors earlier this summer, but the deal had been put on hold pending the completion of the NBA’s investigation. Leonard is due to make $50m in salary this season, while Ballmer, the former CEO of Microsoft, has an estimated wealth of $152.7bn, according to Forbes.

articles.title: Walsh caps Champions League progress for Chelsea despite Real Sociedad grind
articles.summary: Real Sociedad 0-1 Chelsea (agg 2-6) Keira Walsh scores at corner to settle tie. Chelsea ensured there will be three Women’s Super League teams in the league phase of the Champions League as Keira Walsh’s second-half strike against Real Sociedad extended their three-goal margin from the first leg of…
body: The 5-2 win against the Spanish side in Chelsea’s first game at Wimbledon’s Cherry Red Records stadium gave Sonia Bompastor’s side a commanding lead in the tie, after a rusty start had forced them to come from a goal down. It wasn’t a particularly pretty performance, though, and that continued into the second leg against La Real, who will now drop into the Europa League.

Bompastor, who returned to the dugout after serving a one-match ban in the reverse game, made four changes for the trip to San Sebastián, probably with one eye on the WSL opener on Saturday against Aston Villa. The scorer of Chelsea’s second last week, Veerle Buurman, was named on the bench, alongside Katie McCabe, Sjoeke Nüsken and Alyssa Thompson. Among those to come in was the 20-year-old midfielder Lexi Potter, who scored in her first league start for Chelsea, a 2-1 win against Brighton, in March.

It was a mountain of a task ­facing the 40-year-old and, in many respects, a bit of a free hit, with few expecting Real Sociedad to come close to overturning a three-goal ­deficit against European heavyweights.

articles.title: Birds stop play but Medvedev flies into third round
articles.summary: An interruption from a pair of birds ruffles Daniil Medvedev's feathers but fails to disrupt the seventh seed as he eases into the US Open third round with a dominant victory over Sebastian Gorzny.
body: The two birds settled down on the net for a closer look at the action midway through a second-set rally, with play continuing around them for several strokes before the chair umpire called for the point to be replayed.

Medvedev, who placed the incident in his "top five" most unusual experiences at the New York major, was visibly stunned by the decision which came just after he thought he had won the point with a cross-court forehand.
"This is very bad," the 2021 champion said as he remonstrated at the umpire on court.

Russia's Medvedev is no stranger to losing his composure on court, notably receiving a fine of almost £31,500 at last year's US Open for an extraordinary meltdown during his first-round defeat to Benjamin Bonzi.

articles.title: Wolves announce signing of defender Konan
articles.summary: Wolves have announced their final signing of the summer transfer window - almost 23 hours after it closed - by bringing in Portugal-based Ivory Coast defender Ghislain Konan.
body: The 30-year-old 57-times capped left-back, who played under new Wolves head coach Cesar Peixoto at Gil Vicente in the Portuguese Liga last season, has signed on a one-year deal.
He fills the gap in the squad left by David Moller Wolfe's departure to SV Hamburg on deadline day.
Konan started his career with Ivorian club ASEC Mimosas before moving to Portugal with Vitoria Guimaraes.

He then moved in 2018 to Stade de Reims, where he spent five years, before a stint in the Saudi Pro League, first at Al-Nassr, then Al-Fayha, half a season with Spanish second tier side Burgos and then last season's time with Gil Vicente.

articles.title: Why Fulham failed to sign Fikayo Tomori on deadline day
articles.summary: Fikayo Tomori is set to be reinstated into the first-team squad at Milan, having failed to agree terms with Fulham. As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport, the English defender was in London recently with his agents to discuss terms over a move to Fulham, but the West London outfit did not manage…
body: Tomori is now back at Milanello, where he’s expected to rejoin Ruben Amorim’s squad. The Portuguese coach had made it clear to Tomori throughout pre-season that he could leave, but he’s happy to welcome him back into the fray, with the 28-year-old also keen to fight for his place at the club. This was communicated to the defender in a phonecall with the Portuguese just after the Fulham move broke down.

The Chelsea academy graduate was subject to interest from several Premier League sides, with with Newcastle United, Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest having considered making a move for him before Fulham entered the fray.

That Milan did not manage to sign another centre-back is another key reason for Tomori’s quick reintegration into the squad. He’s even going to take back his #23 shirt. Matteo Gabbia’s recent issues with an ankle discomfort could even see him make the bench against Juventus on Sunday.
Tomori loves Milan. He has said no to moves away from San Siro in the past, including a high-profile one to rivals Juventus, and is keen to make the most of what chances he gets this season.

articles.title: Former Detroit Lions Cornerback Alphonso Smith Jr. Dies
articles.summary: has died at the age of 40, according to a report Wednesday from TMZ Sports. Sources with direct knowledge of the situation told TMZ Sports that Smith died by suicide Wednesday in Florida.
body: Smith spent three seasons with the Lions from 2010 through 2012 after beginning his NFL career with the Denver Broncos.

According to TMZ, Smith posted an emotional message to Facebook before his death in which he described struggling with what he called “demons,” apologized to people he believed he had hurt and said he had needed help.

“Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME! I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It’s EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it!”
TMZ reported that Smith continued apologizing in the post and referenced abuse he said he suffered from an older woman when he was a child.

articles.title: Boulter blown away by Muchova at US Open
articles.summary: Katie Boulter suffered a nightmare US Open exit in a punishing straight sets defeat to Karolina Muchova in under an hour at Flushing Meadows.
body: The British No 1 was broken in all seven of her service games in a chastening 6-1 6-0 defeat inside 58 minutes on Louis Armstrong Stadium.
Boulter traded breaks with Muchova at the start of the first set only for the 2026 Wimbledon finalist to pull clear and put on a clinic for her beleaguered opponent.
Boulter double faulted eight times and produced 22 unforced errors in a nightmare, error-strewn performance that left her hopes of progressing in tatters.

"It was a tough day at the office for Boulter, and that is where Muchova deserves so much credit. She is such an all-round player. The focus was definitely on Muchova rather than what Boulter didn't do.

But having soaked up waves of pressure - Campbell fired home from close range after 69 minutes to earn a point for his side.
